Subject: PrivDeploy pricing - follow up & procurement checklist

Kimberly / Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has asked us to get a clearer picture on two things before we loop legal in: (1) whether Redwood can split the commercial construct between a platform fee and a per-node operator license (we want the ability to ramp nodes independently), and (2) how support tiers map to response SLAs and on-call coverage (our SREs will be 24/7).

Two asks from our side: can you provide a simple cost scenario comparing (A) 1x annual platform fee + per-node operator SKU and (B) a blended per-node + reduced platform fee (we have ~25 nodes in year 1, ~60 in year 2), and an explanation of what triggers an SLA uplift charge?

If you can send a short summary + a term sheet stub, we can expedite procurement/legal review.

Best,
Liam

Hi Liam —

Thanks — copying David (pricing) and Marissa (customer success) so we can put numbers and the operational checklist in one package.

Quick summary up front: we can do both constructs. High level differences:
- Option A (Platform-first + operator SKU): Predictable base platform revenue, lower marginal operator cost; simpler billing for multi-site deployments.
- Option B (Blended per-node + reduced platform fee): Lower entry platform fee, higher marginal cost as you scale nodes, better for customers who expect modest long-term node growth.

We have two deliverables inbound: (1) simple scenario spreadsheet (per your node counts) and (2) a term-sheet stub that shows platform fee, operator SKU price, and a support-tier mapping (Standard / Enhanced / Enterprise). We will also call out what constitutes an SLA uplift (major incident with customer-facing downtime, ~>1% sustained error rate, or agreed on-call augmentation beyond the contracted hours).

Drafts attached: Redwood_PrivDeploy_TermSheet_v1.pdf (term points + concessions) and PrivDeploy_Cost_Scenarios_2026-04.xlsx (scenario A vs B).

I'll follow up with a short note describing the support tier commitment windows.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Kim / David —

Forwarding Liam's note and the attachments Kim dropped in. A couple of items from the CS/ops side for pricing negotiation and procurement checklist:

1) Support tiers detail:
   - Standard: business-hours (M-F 8am-6pm local) support, 24-hr ticket SLA for P1, no guaranteed phone on-call.
   - Enhanced: 24/7 ticketing + phone on-call during business hours, 4-hr P1 response objective, escalation to engineering for infra-impacting incidents.
   - Enterprise: 24/7 phone on-call + named SRE, 2-hr P1 response objective, quarterly on-site review (optional).

2) Suggested commercial concessions to close:
   - Year 1: reduce platform fee by 10% if Medivault signs a 24-month commitment and hits a minimum 20-node commit by month 6.
   - Migration credit: one-time implementation credit that offsets up to 3 months of platform fee for new on-prem clusters (conditional on deployment schedule).
   - SLA credit cap: max service credit of 10% of monthly platform fee per incident (to limit open-ended exposure).

3) Procurement asks we should be prepared for: extended payment terms, detailed audit logging/observability add-on pricing, and a request for a carveout for air-gapped environments (we should treat that as a separate charge).

Notes to David: can you sanity-check the numbers in the spreadsheet (I highlighted the Year 1 blended scenario vs platform-first) and confirm our margin at those price points? If margin falls below 30% in the blended scenario, flag it.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync with Liam + Eileen Friday if needed.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy pricing - follow up & procurement checklist

Liam / Eileen —

Appreciate the clear asks. We've attached a short term-sheet stub and two cost scenarios (A and B) for your procurement team. Highlights and our proposed commercial compromise: 

- Proposed path: start with Option B (reduced platform fee + per-node operator SKU) for Year 1 to lower your entry point, with an automatic true-up at Year 2 based on node count thresholds (25/50/100). True-up protects Redwood's margin while allowing you predictable ramp flexibility.

- Migration credit: 2 months of platform fee credited against the first invoice if onboarding completes within the agreed 90-day window.

- Support mapping: we recommend Enhanced as the default for Medivault (24/7 ticketing + phone on-call during business hours, 4-hr P1 objective). Enterprise (2-hr P1 + named SRE) is available as an add-on. SLA uplift charges apply only if we provide augmented on-call beyond contracted hours or deliver dedicated engineering time.

- Risk cap: service credit max 10% monthly platform fee per qualifying incident; cumulative annual cap at 25% of annual platform fee.

Next steps: if this aligns, we'll (a) update the term-sheet to reflect the Year 1/Year 2 true-up language, (b) ask legal to prepare a procurement-friendly SOW with the migration credit and SLA cap language, and (c) schedule a 30-min call next week to confirm technical on-call handoffs (please suggest times).

If you'd like, Marissa can prep a one-page operational checklist for the SOW that flags observability and audit-log expectations.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Enterprise — Redwood Inference
